purpose: Ensures clear ownership of AI risk decisions so that responsibility doesn't diffuse across teams with no one actually accountable.
summary: Accountability structures are in place so that the appropriate teams and individuals are empowered, responsible, and trained for mapping, measuring, and managing AI risks, including documented roles, AI risk management training, and executive-level accountability for AI system risk decisions.
expectedStatementElements: How roles, responsibilities, and communication lines for AI risk are documented
What AI risk management training personnel and partners receive
How executive leadership is involved in and accountable for AI risk decisions
How accountability is enforced when AI risk responsibilities aren't met
evidenceExamples: RACI matrix or org chart showing AI risk roles and responsibilities
AI risk management training curriculum and completion records
Executive sign-off records on AI system risk acceptance decisions
Escalation path documentation for AI risk issues
commonGaps: AI risk responsibilities are informally understood but not documented anywhere
No training exists specifically covering AI risk management
Executive leadership isn't involved in AI risk decisions until something goes wrong
No clear escalation path exists when an AI risk issue is identified
interviewQuestions: Who is accountable for AI risk decisions, and is that documented anywhere?
What training do people who work with AI systems receive on managing AI risk?
At what point does executive leadership get involved in an AI risk decision?
What happens if an AI risk issue gets identified but nobody acts on it?
